fields.population: residents and municipal officials of the City of Johannesburg (sanitation and service delivery); number of participants not stated
fields.sample_size: not stated: the paper reports a qualitative approach with residents and officials, informed consent and confidentiality, but gives no number of participants, sampling method or instrument; the larger part of the text is literature review and policy discussion
fields.effect_measure: qualitative description of municipal conduct, ward-committee effectiveness and ICT governance for sanitation service delivery; no systematic coding or quantitative measure reported
fields.effect_estimate: Reported findings: unethical behaviour and relative deprivation contribute to failures and imbalances in ward committees and municipal structures; residents in urban centres are said to receive better amenities than those in areas with fewer amenities; services such as sanitation and refuse collection are comparatively poor and trigger protests; limited ward-councillor responsiveness; public participation promotes effective provision. Recommends municipal ICT governance (e-government under the Batho Pele principles), awareness raising and transparency. No data shown to support the findings.
fields.model_type: qualitative description with extensive literature and policy review; no analytic method named
fields.study_design: qualitative study (design and sample not described) combined with policy and literature review

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a short qualitative paper (6 pp) on municipal conduct, ward committees and ICT governance for sanitation in Johannesburg, read in full text 2026-10-04. Mostly literature and policy discussion; the empirical component has no stated sample, instrument or analysis, so its findings cannot be checked. Weak reporting.

notes: Very thin methods (no sample); keep but treat as low-confidence evidence; E09-style insufficient-information exclusion is arguable.
